links.reason: 2616 says only that the span of days is unknown and cannot be recalled (இறந்தநாள் யாவர்மீட்பார்); 2748 merely lists topics (அருமையின் எய்தும் யாக்கை, யாக்கைய தழிவு). Nothing shows the sermon taking up her points, so the link is a shared theme.

416 foretells that after the raiders win the herd they will be broken 'ஒருவன் தேரினால் உடைதும்'; 449 shows the hunters shrinking at 'வள்ளல் தேர் முழக்கினான்'. A prophecy and its fulfilment, which is a real develops link.
links.text_issue: 416 line 4 is hard to divide and may be corrupt.

links.reason: 1827 has the kings calm themselves with 'வினைகள் விளையும் ஆறு... வினையதால்'; ND33 sets the fool who sighs against those who say 'தொல்லையது'. Same idea, but the named 'fool' opposite and the appeal to 1826 are not in the packet, so teaches and gains are generic.

24 has the friend point to the rain as the sign 'வருகுறியால்' of him who swore 'வஞ்சினம்'; 1154 asks who is at fault if the one who said 'அஞ்சல்' leaves. The claim that the Kural names a risk the friend 'leaves unsaid' is the grader's inference, not in the Tamil of either.

2679 has the moon waste before her face (மதி... தேய்ந்தது); 1118 tells the moon it would be loved if it shone like her face. Same face-moon conceit, but 'ends her sulk' is read into the verse and the epic gains only a pedigree.

118 is Turumakanthan going to the garden (தொழுதுசெல்); 116 is the ministers' proposal to post him (காவல் வைத்தும்). That is plot order. The 'king's approval' that the teaches rests on is in neither verse.

2904 reasons 'பொள்ளல் இவ் உடம்பு' and calls for the heir; 642 says gold stays when Yama takes the body. Neither Yama nor a throne nor any descent from one is in 2904, so 'acts on the warning' is imported; the link is the shared theme that the body fails.
links.text_issue: Lines 2-3 of 2904 (the tusk and thunder similes) are obscure.

links.reason: 356 says austerity and knowledge, with the body's 'இகந்துபோம் இயற்கை', lead to 'கடவுட் டானம்'; ND27 has the firm resolve to end தடுமாற்றம் after seeing the body as a bubble. Linking the resolve to a destination is fair, but 'divine seat' is not the ending of birth, and கருமச் சுற்றம் is unclear.
links.text_issue: 356 flagged uncertain; கருமச் சுற்றம் is unclear.

links.reason: 312 gives gold pot broken and made a crown with the gold remaining (செம்பொன் நிலையுதலும் சிதைவாக்கம்) applied to 'நரர் தேவர் உயிர்கள்'; MM 183-186 gives the neem and the gram cooked into கும்மாயம் with the kind unchanged. Same persistence-in-change doctrine in two different examples, and the Jain asserts it in Neelakesi.

185 has wounded men anointed (நெய் மருந்து பூசவும்) and given wealth; 546 says victory comes from the sceptre that does not bend (கோடாது). Care for the wounded is not the straightness of the sceptre, and the verse does not claim it as ruling by dharma.

894 has Suramanjari's powder fall and Gunamalai's taken by bees; 2077 has her mother say 'கரி விளைத்து... சுண்ணம் வாட்டினன்' and call the chastity kept for him. The callback is real but 2077's line 2 (பெருவளைப் பிட்டுக் காத்த) is obscure, and the vow came from the verdict, not the bees.

84 has 'வேளை இது என்று கொண்டு விரகினால் கயிறு பற்றி' (hour, means); 483 says nothing is hard to one who knows time and means. It shows the rule; the cost to the innocent is not in the verse, and its closing lines are uncertain.

1561 resolves 'கடிவினை காணலுற்றாள்'; 1621 sets the parijata as bridegroom and begins 'கடிவினை தொடங்கலுற்றார்'. The wish is carried out, but the 'quarrel and its mending' in the teaches is in neither verse.

2758 has death cut men down 'தெரிவில் போகத்து' as kin beat their faces; ND25 has the funeral drum answer the one who marries and says 'உண்டு'. Same memento mori, but the 'voice of the one who watches and does not learn' is not in 2758, so the first gain is invented.

821 has the king embrace his sons (புல்லினான்); 65 calls the touch of children joy to the body. The verse names no joy (its களிதல் is a likely slip), so the 'royal question set aside' is imported and the epic only illustrates.

1842 says the austerity that bore these pleasures 'இன்னும் வித்திடற் பாலது'; 1851 has fools abandon 'நல்வினை முதல்' and die. The sowing and root images are shared, but 1851 does not speak of an unsown field and its sense is uncertain.

454 has the herd turned by the bow's twang (சிலையின் னொலியால்... மீட்டு); P257 is a vetchi poem in which a man 'சிலையின் மாற்றியோனே'. The Puram man is a raider and the epic a recoverer, and 'rests on an existing type' is a claim of derivation the Tamil does not support.
2388 has the proclaimers set on an elephant to drum the wedding; 1687 has the wedding drums sounding for Kanakamalai. These are different weddings, so 2388 is not 'how it is done' for 1687.

1473 uses the rare word தாக்கணங்கு and puns on அணங்கு ('நோக்கணங்காய்'); Kural 1082 has 'நோக்கெதிர் நோக்குதல் தாக்கணங்கு தானைக்கொண்டன்னது'. The shared word and the returned look are exact, and the epic extends the image into a three-way pun while leaving the doubt open.

275 has the king reflect that pleasure and youth pass and aim for 'போகமிகு பொன்னுலகு'; ND53 has the best renounce 'தாம் உய்யக்கொண்டு'. The qualification that the same reflection may end in heaven is real, but the epic does not gain a view from ND53 and line 3 is damaged.

1296 has the crowd guess 'விஞ்சையர் வீரன்... விண்ணவர் குமரன்'; 1311 has Padumai ask whether he is 'காமனோ' or the dark-hill god, saying 'அறியேன்'. The same puzzle in two voices, but the lovesick point in the teaches is the grader's gloss, not a fulfilment of 1296.

303 is Vijayai left in the skull forest, framed 'உண்டு என உரையில் கேட்பார்... பாவம் எல்லாம் கண்டு'; 2338 is the usurper's women walking on 'வெறுவெந்நிலம்'. Both are falls from comfort, but 2338 names no sin and no burning ground, so the mirror is the reader's.

1488 has the Vidyadharas bow saying 'அஞ்சினம்'; 1489 has the hero show mercy to 'அஞ்சிய மன்னர்'. The answer to the fear is stated, but these are adjacent verses in story order, which is sequence rather than development.

1583 gives hair as 'வளி பித்து ஐ... இறைச்சி என்பு... குடர்கள் புன்தோல் நரம்பொடு வழும்பு'; ND46 lists குடரும் கொழுவும்... தோலும் தடியும் வழும்பும். The list overlaps strongly, but 'another man's wife' and the adultery use are not in the verse, and the listing is not shown to be a precedent.

450 has the women's eyes outdo the deer's (மதர்த்த வாட்கண்); 1085 asks whether the look is death, an eye or a doe. The deer-eye comparison is common, and the verse has no three-fold look; its deer reading rests on a garbled line 4.

1109 opens 'நோற்றிலர் மகளிர்'; 270 says the lack of the many is because 'நோலாதவர் பலர்'. The shared நோல் root is real, and applying the rule to losing a beloved is a fair extension, but it is a reported lament, not a development of the Kural's claim about poverty.

2014 says knowledge gained by hearing 'நூற்பொருள் கேட்டு' clears the darkness; 423 says wisdom is seeing the true thing in whatever is heard. They are compatible, and the verse says nothing of trusting the speaker, so the 'check' the gains gives the epic is read in.

320 lists Charanas who go through the air; SP 10 shows a Charana who knows the minds of the travellers ('சிந்தை விளக்கில் தெரிந்தோன்'). Charana is a class of ascetics, not one person, and merging the two powers into one figure rests only on the name.
2467 has drums and conches roar as the groom takes the water (முரசொடு முழங்கி); ND23 turns 'மணப்பறை' into 'பிணப்பறை'. The verse has no irony or warning; the reversal is brought to it by the reader.

2842 says gifts to 'அடங்கலர்' bring strange births; 221 calls only giving to 'வறியார்' true giving. The sage never says the destitute are unworthy, and the Kural does not rank restraint, so the 'opposite answers' are different questions.

2555 has the people cite his birth in the burning ground and rise and ask 'என்னை தவம் செய்யாது'; 304 gives the birth with lamps and the deities bowing. The callback is real, but the teaches calls the birth 'desolation' while 304 shows it as glory.

297 has the usurper take the kingdom and 'பூமகளை எய்தினான்'; 2343 has 'அவன் மக்களுந் தானும் பட்டார்', so the question of who wore the fillet has no answer. A claim of fortune and its reversal is stated by the Tamil.

22 has the woman ask if he praised her teeth only while they were like 'முல்லை முகை'; ND45 has the renunciant refuse those who call smiles 'முல்லை முகை' after seeing fallen teeth. The shared bud image is real, but the poems do not make incompatible claims, and 'bind him for life' is a doubtful reading of lines 19-22.

3039 has kin and followers drop 'பற்று ஆவம் செற்றம்' and become ascetics; it does not speak of release or deny a god. TM 497 has those who 'சிவமாகி... மலம் செற்றோர்' be free; it does not mention grace. No incompatible claim about release is stated in either verse.

2706 has the sons learn 'கலைகள் படைநவின்றார்'; 61 praises children 'அறிவறிந்த'. Different senses of knowing; the couplet is about children's worth, and the verse gives no moral weighing, so the pair is only the shared word.

2846 says the three together burn the tree of deeds (வினைமரம் சுட்டிட) and the 'அநந்த நான்மை' follows; 3082 has the 'காதிப்போர் மன்னர்' fall and 'நான்மைக் கொடி' lifted. The doctrine of one verse is fulfilled in the hero's omniscience in the other.

1585 blames 'காப்பியக் கவிகள்' for dressing the skin bag; ND44 refuses those who call eyes lilies, carp and spears. The point about the genre is real and true to the Tamil, but ND44's praisers are 'கண்ணில்புன் மாக்கள்', not poets, so the quatrain gains no such identification.
333 says wealth is 'அற்கா இயல்பிற்று'; 753 calls it 'பொய்யா விளக்கம்'. One speaks of its staying, the other of its working, so they are compatible and the second does not deny the first.

1037 has lotuses bloom drinking the feet's beauty, and 1038 has them with bees singing; the two stanzas repeat each other, line 2 and 3 almost word for word. The added sound of bees is a small variant, not a development.
links.text_issue: Lines 2 and 3 of each are near duplicates.

links.reason: 2255 has Ulokapalan pull the arrow from his own brow and the blood 'ஒற்றைமாக் கதிர்'; 774 has the hero pull the spear from his body and 'நகும்'. The plucked weapon is shared, but the epic has no laugh and its splendour is the poet's simile, and the pairing does not need the claimed 'stock act'.

77 says the land is a place for those who do penance and make wealth; 731 defines a land as where 'விளையுள் தக்கார் செல்வர்' gather. The verse has neither விளையுள் nor தக்கார், and the 'worthy' reading is imported; one verse does not fill the definition.

1541 has the festival's smoke darken the streets so that the elephant's eyes are lamps; 1544 has the sun, dimmed by 'அகிற்புகை', set. The same hyperbole is carried on, but the two are near-adjacent verses in order and add no more than the sequence.

917 has the prince seat Maruci on a golden-browed elephant; 933 has the king mount the dressed elephant. They are different riders and elephants, and 'courtesy in order of rank' is not in either verse.
